defects.what: The injection probe was validated only on contrasting pairs where BOTH halves contain a query, command or path. It was never measured on lines with no such sink, and it over-fires badly there. My adversarial inputs, run through the demo's exact scan and edit code paths: (1) clean-math.ts, a file with zero security relevance -> `return n + suffix;` scores 0.825 and becomes the file's only marker, severity `error`, message "injection · security risk 83%" (precision 0% on that file); (2) logs.ts, plain logging concatenation -> `const line = "user=" + userId + " action=" + action;` scores 0.947 and is marked `error`, plus two more markers at 0.93 and 0.85. Both paths fail: the scan rule (SCAN_FLOOR 0.70 + top-relative SCAN_GAP) has no guard for a file whose top line is benign, and the edit path's absolute RAISE 0.75 is below both scores. "Lint my edits" is a shipped button and is auto-enabled by "Type it for me", so a visitor typing ordinary string concatenation gets a confident red security error. Seed-file answers are right (6 hit / 1 extra / 2 missed = 86% precision, 75% recall, exactly as the page claims), but the demo is an editable editor and the failure is one keystroke away.
defects.fix: Gate a probe marker on a cheap deterministic sink check before the probability is consulted, so the model only does the job its pairs proved it can do (separate string-built from parameterised AMONG lines that run a query/command/path). heuristics.ts already carries the regexes: add `hasSink(line, lang)` to markers.ts (query keywords inside a string literal, exec/system/Command/subprocess/psql, open/path.join/filepath.Join) and in `markersFromAnswers` drop any `scored` entry whose ref text has no sink before `keep` is computed. Re-run `node src/demos/jev-lint/smoke.mjs --files --typed` to confirm the seed numbers are unchanged, and add a no-sink negative block to the PAIRS table in smoke.mjs (e.g. `return n + suffix;`, `const line = "user=" + userId;`) so a future wording change that reopens this fails the script.

defects.what: Reduction vs the brief: 4 of the 6 original Jev questions are gone (probable_bug, misleading_name, dead_or_unreachable, performance_smell). Only security_risk (as the `injection` probe) and severity (/classify) ship. I independently re-tested the justification with my own statement wordings over the same contrasting pairs and it holds: a probable_bug statement scored the off-by-one 0.943 vs its fix 0.961 (d -0.018), `i <= len(xs)` 0.939 vs 0.953 (d -0.014), `len(ordered) / 2` 0.988 vs 0.985 (d +0.003); a misleading_name statement scored `isEmpty = length > 0` 0.613 vs its fix 0.703 (d -0.090). The model genuinely does not separate these on single lines. The drop is measured, disclosed on the page, disclosed in code comments, and the reveal panel greys the unjudged rows instead of counting them as misses, so this is honest reduction rather than a silent one.
defects.fix: No code change required. Optionally extend smoke.mjs --pairs to actually run one candidate statement per dropped kind and print its (non-)separation, so the page's "no wording separated them" claim is re-measured by the script instead of only asserted in prose.

defects.what: runScan pools both batches into one ranking (allRefs/allAnswers accumulated across batches, then a single markersFromAnswers(..., "scan") call) and applies SCAN_MAX=3 and the top-relative SCAN_GAP across the pool. This contradicts the rationale written in markers.ts three lines above the constants: "its level is not comparable between calls". A 64-line file therefore gets at most 3 markers total, and batch 2's lines compete against batch 1's scale. deploy.sh (48 sendable lines, 2 batches) misses the planted L33 partly for this reason.
defects.fix: Select per batch, then merge: call markersFromAnswers once per batch inside the loop (as flushEdits already does) and union the results, or keep pooling but scale each batch's probabilities to its own max before ranking. Re-run `node src/demos/jev-lint/smoke.mjs --files` and update the precision/recall sentence in src/pages/jev-lint.astro if the numbers move.

defects.what: clusterMarkers(gap=2) demotes a genuinely distinct second defect to `info` when it lands within two lines of a stronger one with the same kind. Since only one kind now ships, every marker shares a kind, so any two defects two lines apart collapse. Reproduced: in my mixed.py probe, `q = "SELECT ... '%s'" % name` (L6, 0.956) and `open("/etc/app/" + req["tpl"])` (L8, 0.763) are two independent injections, and L8 was demoted to info — which also removes it from the findings list and from the precision/recall count.
defects.fix: Now that KINDS has one entry, cluster on adjacency only when the lines are contiguous: change the default `gap` from 2 to 1 in clusterMarkers, or require the demoted line's probability to be within about 0.10 of the primary's before demoting.

defects.what: The contract asks for when_true/when_false hints "of similar length". PROBES[0].when_true is 24 words; when_false is 40 words and carries three distinct escape clauses. The asymmetry is part of what makes the probe cheap to satisfy in the false direction on sink-free lines (see the major defect above).
defects.fix: Trim when_false to roughly when_true's length, e.g. "The outside value is handed over separately as a bound parameter (?, %s, $1) or its own argument. Or the line runs no query, command or path." Re-run `smoke.mjs --pairs` and confirm the 11/12 separation and the seed-file numbers hold.

defects.what: The brief's status bar lists last/p50/p95 latency, decisions per second, judgments per minute, request count, input tokens, tokens per judgment and cost. The .metrics strip has calls, model p50, model p95, round trip p50, tokens, judgments, judgments/min. Missing: last-call latency, decisions per second, tokens per judgment. (Cost was correctly dropped; the brief says to.) The contract's own four required fields are all present, so this is brief drift only.
defects.fix: Add three spans to the .metrics strip: `last` from the newest entry of stats.wall, `tokens/judgment` = stats.tokens / stats.judgments, and `decisions/s` = perMinute(stats.marks) / 60. All three are derivable from state already held.

notes:
Ran in the isolated worktree. The branch was already checked out by another worktree, so I used a detached checkout of origin/demo/jev-lint at f17f126. Nothing modified, nothing pushed; scratch scripts removed and .DS_Store restored.

BUILD: `pnpm build` passes with zero errors (only pre-existing zod/rollup comment warnings). dist/jev-lint/index.html exists; dist/index.html contains "Semantic linter on every keystroke".

SMOKE: `MS_API_KEY=... node src/demos/jev-lint/smoke.mjs` passes all three gates. 32 calls, model p50 649 ms, round trip p50 354 ms, 15,322 input tokens. --pairs: 11 of 12 of the injection probe's own pairs separate (defect 0.76-0.985 vs fixed 0.36-0.74). --files: 6 hits, 1 extra (server.go L33 `fmt.Sprintf("%x", sum)`), 2 misses (server.go L38 shell injection, deploy.sh L33 unquoted rm -rf) = 86% precision, 75% recall, which reproduces the page's claim exactly. --typed: all six typed snippets light up (0.78-0.985). The answers on the seed data are right for the demo's purpose.

CONTRACT: every point holds. meta.ts default export satisfies DemoMeta; Demo.tsx is a default-export React island; demo.css is fully scoped under .d-jev-lint (the only unscoped rule is a @media wrapper) and defines its severity tokens locally while pulling --ink/--line/--mono/--muted/--purple/--sans/--white from site.css; data.ts is deterministic seed data; the .astro page renders Demo with meta, the client:only island and a notes slot carrying a long, accurate "How it works". Batching is texts[] up to 32, one /yes-no plus one /classify per batch, scan capped at MAX_BATCHES=2 (4 calls). No direct fetch in the demo (Demo.tsx goes through dm1() and classifyMany() from src/lib/dm1.ts; the only fetch is in the node smoke script). The .metrics strip has calls, model p50, round trip p50 and tokens. Dm1Error is caught, shown in a .error paragraph, and the batch falls back to regex markers so the editor never blanks. Both auto loops are bounded: autoLint by a 60 s deadline held in a ref (deliberately immune to the baseline switch re-creating flushEdits) and typing by snippet length plus a 60 s stop. Nothing fires on load; tabs and seed files render first and "Scan file" starts the first batch. No new dependencies (package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml untouched); no localStorage; no server code. The diff from merge-base 4df1f8e touches only src/demos/jev-lint/ and src/pages/jev-lint.astro. The branch is pushed to origin.

FAITHFULNESS: the data is a faithful copy. All 40 planted issues carry over (7/7/7/6/6/7) and the six sample texts are identical to /Users/blaget/projects/jev-experiments/jev-lint/src/samples.ts. The original "Type it for me" snippets were not thrown away: they moved to a second button ("Type a probable bug") and a new injection snippet took the primary slot. The interaction loop is complete: six file tabs, full-file scan with a wall-clock burst panel, character typer at the original 38 ms/char, reveal-planted-issues with live precision/recall, reset, the live/regex/+3 s baseline switch, findings list, request log with ok/stale/fallback rows, gutter dots, squiggles, hover probability bars, clusterMarkers, shiftMarkers and stale-answer discard. CodeMirror was replaced by a textarea plus a highlighted overlay, which is the right call under the no-new-deps rule and loses nothing visible. The question set is reduced from 6 to 2, which I verified is a real model limitation rather than a shortcut.

WHY pass=false: the single major defect. The probe is sound inside the domain its pairs cover but unguarded outside it, and the failure is reachable in two clicks on a page whose whole promise is "semantic linter". The fix is roughly ten lines plus a negative block in the smoke script. Every other part of this build is solid and honestly documented.
